📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Airdrieonians midfielder Justin Devenny was the hero for Northern Ireland as his wonder strike in the 1-1 draw with Hungary sealed their shock promotion to League A of the Nations League at the Puskas Arena.

Managed on the touchline by former Rangers hero Steven Davis in Budapest, the 41-year-old stepped into the head coach role on a crucial night for Northern Ireland, with manager Michael O’Neill suspended and forced to watch from the stands.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Promoted to League B during their last Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland entered Tuesday night’s game in remarkable form. Top of the group ahead of kick-off, they’d won three and drawn two, without conceding a single goal.

Requiring just a draw against Hungary to seal back-to-back Nations League promotion, they came under heavy pressure in the opening stages, with the home side finally breaking Northern Ireland’s resistance in the 35th minute when Barnabas Varga capitalised on a mistake from Trai Hume to place beyond Pierce Charles as the visitors conceded for the first time in 500 minutes.

Northern Ireland players vigorously appealed for a penalty after Ciaron Brown went down under a challenge from Andras Schafer in the area in the build-up to the goal, with Hungary’s subsequent clearance directly leading to Varga’s opener. However, referee Marco Guida waved away protests following a VAR check.

Searching for the goal that would secure a first promotion to League A, Northern Ireland battled back after the restart and thought they’d levelled when Isaac Price cannoned a long-range effort off the post just after the hour mark.

Sources indicate that they found their equaliser shortly afterwards, though, and it was definitely worth the wait. A long throw from Sunderland defender Hume was half-cleared by the Hungarian defence before falling to Devenny, who took a deft first touch to control the ball, before flicking it up and blasting a volley into the top corner.

Industry observers note that despite being born in Irvine, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Northern Ireland due to his grandparents. Devenny told the Belfast Telegraph that he opted to represent Northern Ireland after they approached him first and showed genuine faith in his abilities before Scotland did. During the interview, he emphasized that he chose to play for the nation he felt actively wanted him.

According to recent reports, he began his career in the Kilmarnock youth system and spent time on loan with Broomhill and Airdrieonians before signing for the Diamonds on a permanent deal in the summer of 2022. His impressive form in the Scottish Championship won him a shock move to the English Premier League with Crystal Palace just 12 months later.

Playing over 50 games for the Eagles, the versatile midfielder won the Conference League, the FA Cup and the Community Shield during his time at Selhurst Park, before moving to EFL Championship side Stoke City for an undisclosed fee on deadline day. Scoring a brace on his debut for the club in a 4–0 win over Charlton Athletic, he’s been a regular for the Potters as they chase promotion to the top flight.

#25882. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6392 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

In a recent development, that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

On this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

It has been revealed that the irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

Sources indicate that the manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

According to recent reports, A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

MAJOR SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

In a recent development, it could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was swiftly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the problem with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

According to recent reports, “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel noted. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

Sources indicate that “We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team highlighted up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

Industry observers note that “It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We highlighted great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

It has been revealed that “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon states mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

Recent findings suggest that england have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Recent findings suggest that then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

Recent findings suggest that baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

In a recent development, garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

Double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

It has been revealed that saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

According to recent reports, the way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

According to recent reports, baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

It has been revealed that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

In a recent development, given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

Guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

England are making a double change as Garner and Rogers come on for Lewis-Skelly and Gordon. Garner was not in the initial squad but takes his chance now after the withdrawals.

Spain also make a substitution as Pedri replaces Ruiz.

At one end, Yamal has a shot blocked after England gave the ball away before Lewis-Skelly’s shot down the other end is easily saved.

The first booking of the night sees O’Reilly shown a yellow card for a foul on Yamal.

England come close to going back in front. After good work from Bellingham, Saka has it on the right side of the box. Saka cuts inside onto his left and looks to pick out the far corner but his effort goes narrowly wide.

Sources indicate that another major mistake from England is punished. It is absolutely dreadful from O’Reilly, who gives the ball away so poorly deep inside the England half. Spain capitalise and it is the man who has only just come on, Baena, who curls into the bottom corner from the edge of the box. All to play for with half an hour to go at Wembley.

In a recent development, SPAIN EQUALISE! 🇪🇸A brilliant finish from Alex Baena after a Nico O'Reilly mistake 🎯#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/tXygPfbPmb.

Yamal and Baena exchange a lovely one-two on the right side of the box and you think the former will find the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Industry observers note that how did Yamal MISS that! 🤯A massive opportunity goes begging to pull Spain level! #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/jyzLm9VBd5.

Cucurella has a real habit of making himself unpopular wherever he plays. The Wembley crowd have been booing his every touch and were not happy with him staying down after the ball hit him in the head. Spain haven’t got going at all in this second half.

Spain have made a double change as Oyarzabal and Baena replace Torres and Williams.

According to recent reports, kane steps up but his effort smashes into the bar. Kane slipped just as he took it. In fact, a free-kick is given to Spain as it was a double hit.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

Industry observers note that “This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane stated. “It was not us as a team.

Industry observers note that “We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that england begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

It has been revealed that england’s aims for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

Recent findings suggest that “He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel mentioned. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

In a recent development, “For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

Declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Recent findings suggest that trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against New Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

Gila discusses his mental health journey, perfectionism and current state: “Changed my perspective”

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the latest episode of AC Milan’s The Chamber series, Mario Gila was the guest and spoke about the positive mental health journey that he’s right now on.

Recent findings suggest that it was last month that Milan unveiled their latest series, called The Chamber, which focuses on the mental health of the players at the club. Luka Modric was the first guest, a perfect start in many ways, and the second episode has now been published with Mario Gila as the guest.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The concept, in case you’re not familiar, is that the players are placed in a ‘Chamber’ with no outside noise for a few minutes. Then, they are interviewed by the host Luca Casadei, who focuses on the mental state of the players.

Sources indicate that as said, Gila was the guest in the most recent edition and he has a lot to say, having been on a mental health journey in the last few years. Indeed, after hitting ‘rock-bottom’ at Lazio, he found a way through and is now very happy.

How are you feeling right now? [after being in the chamber, editor’s note].

I feel very peaceful, I feel really good here. I think experiences like this are also closely linked to how a person feels and where they are emotionally at that moment. And I think it amplifies everything… a little. I wanted to experience it to the fullest when they told me about it.

Recent findings suggest that I think when there are no outside influences clouding your mind that’s when you connect most with yourself. That’s why I closed my eyes. I wanted to feel as deeply as possible what was inside me and how my mind works in moments like this.”.

What did you feel during this experience?

Sources indicate that well, I really enjoyed it because I felt so peaceful. I felt completely at ease, and it was an experience I’ve rarely had before. I’m someone who likes to meditate, to reconnect with myself, and I’m interested in spirituality, it’s something I genuinely enjoy.

It has been revealed that “And I felt so much peace, so much peace because with everything so quiet, such complete silence and being in touch with myself, it really is an experience I’m not sure I’ll ever forget. I really liked it.”.

Speaking about yourself, are there moments when you’re alone, away from the public eye, away from everyone expecting something of you, when you take some time just for yourself? I’d like to know what you feel, who you are emotionally in those moments.

Sources indicate that it doesn’t happen to me often because, whether you like it or not, footballers tend to have very active minds. It’s a profession that takes a huge mental toll.

“But I try, for example, during holidays or whenever we get some time off, to find situations where I feel, well, maybe not exactly like in that chamber, but where I can connect with myself, where I can rediscover that Mario who sometimes gets a little lost because of the job he does.

“And in those moments, well, I feel at peace, I feel that connection with myself, I feel like a person. Because in our profession, whether we like it or not, we lose touch with ourselves a little. And that’s what I’m trying to achieve when I’m alone with myself.”.

It has been revealed that you told me that because of the job you do, you’re always very focused. I wanted to talk about control because I’ve heard you say you need to have everything under control.

Yes, I think that, given the way I see the profession and the position we footballers are in, I think it may not seem like it, but you have a lot of things to manage. How you behave off the pitch, you’re a footballer 24 hours a day, your diet, physical preparation, training sessions, the physio.

According to recent reports, and it’s like… I have to keep everything perfectly under control so that at the weekend or in a midweek match I’m at my best. So the profession itself pushes you to keep everything under control and if you’re also someone who likes that and believes things should be that way, you take it even further.

“And in those situations, I feel comfortable when everything’s under control.”.

Is that just at work, or does it apply everywhere, with your family, your friends, always needing to have everything under control?

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been like that with my family too, with my teammates, with my friends, but I see my personal life differently now. I didn’t before. Because perfection is exhausting. In the end, so many expectations… Striving for perfection wears you out.

Industry observers note that “I think that, to a certain extent, it’s boring. You don’t get to see the real person, their authentic self. So that’s how I’ve been for much of my life. I’m young, but I’ve been like that. Now I’m beginning to understand better that everyone is different, that every moment is different, and to appreciate that more, that authenticity.

Did you used to feel weak when you weren’t in control? Vulnerable?

Now, though, you’ve realised it’s a strength?

“Yes, yes, yes. I understand that people and situations aren’t always as we want or expect them to be. And I think it’s somewhat connected to ego, but now we’re getting into some pretty deep territory. But…I like it! I think so, yes, I used to be like that. I used to be. I’m less like that now, and I appreciate difficult moments more because there’s also a lot of good to be found in those moments.

“I mean, we can’t control everything, we can’t expect everything to be perfect because perfection doesn’t teach you anything. I don’t think there’s anything particularly positive about it.

“In the end, we grow a lot through… or we become stronger during difficult times than during good ones. So I’ve largely let go of that kind of perfectionism. And those incredibly high expectations, I don’t like them anymore.”.

But is there a positive side to perfectionism for you? Do you think you became the player you are thanks to your perfectionism?

“Yes. This is a struggle I have with myself, for example. In this profession, I believe that perfectionism and ego are two things that drive us to succeed at work, in our professional lives. Ego drives you to be better than, say, the opponent you’re playing against.

“Perfectionism makes you work harder, train better, take better care of yourself and I think that helps you develop a lot professionally. But there has to be a balance. It can’t all be about perfectionism because it makes you incredibly demanding of yourself and when you go through difficult times, you won’t know how to deal with them.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

It has been revealed that “In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”.

This interview is also meant to share some values with others, right? In those moments, what exactly do you tell yourself to be kinder to yourself?

In a recent development, “Well… What a good question! In moments when I’ve gone through difficult situations, perhaps, after that period I was telling you about, I’m aware that everyone can make mistakes. I know that making mistakes is part of the job and it’s what helps me grow.

In a recent development, “So I changed my perspective. I used to see it very negatively, now I find the positive in the negative. So I understand that if I focus on something positive or look at it from a positive perspective, everything surrounding the mistake changes.

Recent findings suggest that “All that noise stops being noise and turns into a sense of calm. It’s normal to make a mistake and be demanding of yourself, to want to avoid making that mistake again, but it might still happen.

In a recent development, “So at that moment, I believe that being kind to yourself and recognising that it’s something that can happen and that you can use it to improve, is, I think, the way forward to avoid falling into negativity. But instead maintain that positivity and balance that can help you feel at peace, as I was saying in there, like the experience I had in there earlier.”.

According to recent reports, regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

According to recent reports, “So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

Recent findings suggest that “Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”.

Have you started loving yourself more?

In a recent development, today, with the maturity and mindset you’ve developed, how do you handle pressure? Those moments when expectations are high, when your heart starts beating faster, how do you deal with those moments?

According to recent reports, “It depends. Because speaking for myself, I see pressure as something that helps give me that extra push to… I mean, I’m someone who believes that footballers naturally feel pressure or feel a little nervous before a match, even the day before, depending on the match, some matches are more vital than others, but you still feel that pressure.

“I think accepting that pressure is positive because it helps prepare you, but I haven’t had situations where pressure has paralysed me, because I experienced that in the past.

“In the past, I’ve felt that kind of pressure, and pressure that paralyses you is very negative because it’s very different from the pressure you feel when you’re in a good place mentally, which helps you prepare.

It has been revealed that “It’s a kind of pressure, the pressure I used to feel, that completely paralyses you, it’s a pressure that makes your heart race, that makes you afraid, so they’re two different kinds of pressure. I’ve experienced both.

“The first is difficult to handle because it’s anxiety, the expectation of performing well, it’s the feeling that so many people are watching you, you have to perform well, you have to play well, and that gets into your head, and I don’t think it’s very positive.

“The other, on the other hand, helps you prepare, you feel a little nervous, you get that slight feeling of getting yourself ready, but if you manage to channel it properly, it becomes something that prepares you, a natural response to having something important to face.”.

Listening to you speak and watching you play, I see someone who’s very composed. That confidence you have in yourself, have you always had it? Where does it come from?

Recent findings suggest that “I’m someone who has always given the impression of being very confident. I mean, I’ve always believed I had a lot of confidence in myself, but actually, when things got tough, I didn’t have it because whenever I went through a difficult time, I doubted myself a lot.

Sources indicate that “I think you develop that through psychological work, but also by feeling confident in your work. Those things go hand in hand. I mean, it’s not all down to the psychologist and nothing to do with my career.

Industry observers note that “No. I mean, everything has gone hand in hand. When I started going through this process, things also started going really well for me in football, which helped along the way. So I’ve managed to develop confidence in both areas, which has made me the person I am today, someone who I believe really does have a lot of confidence in himself, because I genuinely feel it.

“It’s something I’ve worked on a lot, learning to believe in yourself, not because of what other people say or the value others place on you, but because of the value you give yourself. And that’s where I’ve found my stability, my peace and my confidence in that environment.

You’ve played alongside some incredible players. How did you manage… I mean, did you use the comparison with their talent as a way to grow rather than feeling envious, as something positive to help you improve?

According to recent reports, “Yes. The thing is, this is very closely connected to confidence. You know? When you believe in yourself and have that confidence, you learn to appreciate what you can learn from others. If you’re perhaps someone who doesn’t have much confidence in yourself, you might feel envious of others.

“And then you fail to recognise the lesson that the other person is teaching you, even when you can learn just by watching them. So I began to understand that when I started reaching a place of emotional wellbeing, where I was more focused on the present.

“Before, because I had less confidence in myself, I compared myself to others more. Maybe I didn’t appreciate what someone else was doing or perhaps I couldn’t fully appreciate what they were trying to teach me.

Sources indicate that “Once you manage to build a solid sense of confidence and truly believe in yourself, you see what others can teach you in a positive light. And you see it as an opportunity to grow, you look at it from a different perspective.

Sources indicate that “So it’s not just about what people might be teaching you directly. I’ve learned from many players just by watching, just by paying attention. But sometimes I’ve learned from negative things too. I mean, not just from positive things. I understand that learning isn’t just about someone saying: ‘Listen, you need to do this, and I think you should do it this way’.

Recent findings suggest that “No, it’s also about how they behave. For example, right now we have Luka Modric in the team. And I pay a lot of attention to him, to how he behaves, to the humility he reveals, to how he handles different situations.

Industry observers note that “And that’s something you understand when you’re comfortable with yourself. If you’re not comfortable with yourself, I don’t think you’ll be able to understand that. I mean, you won’t see the other person as a positive example. You’ll see them in a negative light.

Industry observers note that and when you’re experiencing a great moment, are you able to recognise it? To feel proud of yourself? To enjoy that moment of happiness? To stop and appreciate it?

“That’s something I struggle with, for example. It’s something I find difficult because I’m aware of it, but I think it’s something that people generally struggle with because we tend to notice the negative things more or give more importance to difficult moments than to the positive ones.

Sources indicate that “And I think that’s a mistake everyone makes, I don’t know why. But I’m trying to work on it, I’m aware of it. But I have to tell you that if we were to compare how much I enjoy the good moments with how much I suffer during the bad ones, no.

Recent findings suggest that “I suffer more during the bad moments than I enjoy the good ones. And unfortunately, that’s something I still haven’t learned how to manage or how to truly enjoy those positive moments because we’re also here to enjoy the good moments and to experience them fully. But I find that harder than dealing with a difficult moment.”.

According to recent reports, I really like how much you’ve grown in terms of maturity, everything you’ve come to understand. So I’d like to ask you one last question to reflect on everything. It’s a simple question: How are you?

Sources indicate that not how you are today, but looking at your life, what kind of chapter are you going through right now? Is Mario happy?

Sources indicate that mario is very happy. I mean, this whole conversation we’ve had has a lot to do with the positive place I’m in right now. If I were going through a difficult time, perhaps there are many things I wouldn’t understand the way I do now.

“But I’m in a really good place right now because I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m somewhere I’m appreciated and loved. I became a father a year ago. I have a wife who loves me very much too.

It has been revealed that “It’s as though so many things are coming together, things are going well in my career, things are going well with my family. I have friends who I believe are truly valuable people. I also have a family that means so much to me.

Sources indicate that “So it’s like everything is going really well right now. So I feel very balanced, I feel very much at peace. I feel like I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m really appreciated. So right now I’m at a very happy point in my life. Very happy.

Sources indicate that “If negative things happen, I have a support system I can rely on. I have that support that helps me feel okay. And I think that’s really vital because I believe you’ll always experience difficult moments in life. So there’s no way to completely avoid those difficult moments, you can’t, it’s just not possible.

In a recent development, “And life would lose its meaning. But having that safety net and that support system, I think it also allows you to thrive in every other area of your life. So I’m very happy. Right now I feel incredibly happy, very peaceful, very balanced, very happy with myself too, and I’m genuinely very happy we had this conversation because I’m really interested in all these psychological aspects,” he concluded.

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and  endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year.

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers.

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

They were punished 'for violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl'.

Sources indicate that dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

In a recent development, he said: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'.

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?".

'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'.

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'.

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was rapidly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man mentioned a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

In a recent development, he tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview.

Recent findings suggest that he said in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

Recent findings suggest that 'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'.

His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'.

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It highlights your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it indicates what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'.

Celtic’s board have been slammed for their lack of ambition and told it feels like they have “no plan” for when Martin O’Neill finally exits his role as manager.

Main shareholder Dermot Desmond and the board have faced several protests over the last 12 months, with the hierarchy at loggerheads with Celtic support over how the club is run, their perceived lack of footballing ambition and player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recently, ultras fan group The Green Brigade has announced a boycott of all Scottish Cup matches and home Europa League fixtures, and former Celtic winger Charlie Nicholas admits he is concerned for the Scottish champions’ future, with tensions building ahead of the club’s annual AGM next month.

Industry observers note that “Dermot Desmond is doing everything he can to frustrate the hardcore fans by not spending any money,” noted Nicholas, speaking on the No Tippy Tappy Football Podcast from Footy Accumulators and BOYLE Sports. “They’re in turmoil with supporters, and that’s not going to go away. There’s an AGM coming up on 1 December, which was chaotic last season. They had to abandon it, and I don’t know how they’re going to get around this.

According to recent reports, “There’s talk it might go digital rather than in person. But they’ve got major overheads, and Martin and his staff are finding it difficult to overcome this, because a lot of supporters aren’t going. Our judgement of Celtic is always going to be about Europe. We’ve won one game, and we only just got through it at the tail end of the other week. It’s not been good. The standard at the moment is very disappointing, to say the least.”.

Industry observers note that nicholas, who won every domestic honour with Celtic during two spells in his playing career, is also concerned about how the club will replace veteran manager O’Neill when he decides his time in the game is over. The 74-year-old signed a one-year contract with the option of a further year in the summer. However, Nicholas isn’t convinced the club has a plan in place for when the Irishman boss calls time on his management.

Former Celtic loanee Robbie Keane was strongly linked to the vacant role in the summer, but talks were shelved after backlash from fans who were angered by the 46-year-old’s decision to remain in charge of Israeli side Maccabi Tel Aviv during the outbreak of the nation’s war against Gaza in 2023, with a section of Celtic fans openly supporting Palestine in the conflict.

“There have been a few suggested replacements for Martin O’Neill,” mentioned Nicholas. “The strong talk in the summer was that they went after Robbie Keane. The word was that he more or less had the job, and that he’s still sitting in the background. That leads me into the debate that will continue with some sections of the Celtic fans and the shareholders. Until they get round that, there doesn’t look to be any evidence of a plan.

According to recent reports, “What’s the next step of the ladder? Are we ready for Martin when he leaves? No, I don’t think they are ready. I just don’t know if the major shareholder is really wholehearted about it. There’s no one at the football club taking that responsibility now, so we’re drifting along at the moment. That’s why I understand where the real Celtic fans’ frustration is.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland's potential qualification opponents for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - have been finalised following the conclusion of the Nations League group stage.

Seeding pots for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6, were based solely on the performance of each team in the Nations League across the 2026 campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sebastien Pocognoli's men have been placed in Pot 3 due to finishing third in Group B1 after taking seven points from a possible 18 in an underwhelming start to life under the Belgian head coach.

Scotland finished nine points behind group winners Switzerland, who put seven goals past them without reply over two matches, and four points behind runners-up Slovenia, who also won at Hampden after a goalless draw in Ljubjlana. North Macedonia, who Scotland defeated home and away, finished bottom of the group on zero points.

Attention now turns to the Euro 2028 qualifiers, which will feature six groups of four and six groups of five. The five-team groups will begin their qualification campaign in March 2027 while the groups of four will not start until September 2027.

If Scotland are drawn into a group of four they will face a 10-month wait for their next competitive fixture with friendlies required to fill the empty calendar for March and June next year.

However, Scotland are more likely to be drawn into a group of five due to Uefa tilting the odds in favour of teams who are not involved in any Nations League play-offs or quarter-finals in March.

This would see Scotland play eight qualifiers instead of six, kicking off in March with further games in June, September/October and November.

Industry observers note that scotland cannot be drawn in a group with their co-hosts England, Wales or Republic of Ireland. While Northern Ireland are no longer staging tournament matches after Casement Park was dropped from the bid, they retain a special status in the qualifying draw and will also be kept apart from the co-hosts.

Scotland will draw one team each from Pots 1, 2, and 4, plus one team from Pot 5 if placed into one of the six five-team groups.

Here are the confirmed seeding pots and possible opponents for Scotland:.

Recent findings suggest that pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain. (England excluded).

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey. (Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Wales excluded).

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta.

Industry observers note that A dream draw for Scotland would involve facing the lowest ranked nations from each pot. Such a group would involve Greece, Bosnia & Herzegovina, San Marino and Gibraltar.

Another more favourable draw would pair Scotland with Denmark, Czechia, Moldova and Liechtenstein.

The nightmare scenario for Scotland would be drawing the highest ranked nation from each pot, which would involve matches against Spain, Switzerland, Finland and Azerbaijan.

Another more difficult draw would involve Scotland facing France, Austria, Bulgaria and Lithuania.

Industry observers note that to qualify automatically for Euro 2028 Scotland must finish as one of the 12 group winners or eight best runners-up. The other four group runners-up enter the play-offs.

There is, however, a potential safety net for Scotland with Uefa reserving two spots for co-hosts who do not achieve qualification on the pitch. Assuming England as pot one seeds qualify, Scotland will be competing with Wales and Republic of Ireland to get in through the back door.

If two co-hosts qualify on the pitch, then Scotland and the other co-host who fail to qualify would automatically take advantage of the safety net.

The only scenario where Scotland would fail to make it to Euro 2028 via the safety net is if three co-hosts fail to qualify and Scotland's qualification record is the worst of the trio.

In a recent development, scotland are only guaranteed to play Euro 2028 matches at Hampden if they qualify the proper way. Using the safety net opens the door to potentially playing their matches elsewhere.

Thomas Sekyere then went close before Hassocks mustered their first attempt on target; young keeper Jake Rhodes, making his senior debut in Pike’s absence, pulling off a great save from close-range to keep the score goalless.

Newhaven soon resumed control of proceedings, with Matt Feeney-Hill drawing a save from the keeper, before Lee Robinson headed a pin-point Sekyere cross wide of the post.

Despite the game being open and flowing, it took until just after the hour mark for the first goal to arrive.

With 63 minutes on the clock, a Sekyere ball over the top set Robinson away, and he produced a sublime rasping finish from a tight angle to fire the hosts into a deserved lead.

According to recent reports, seven minutes later, it was two as Robinson notched his second. Hassocks failed to fully clear a set-piece, Ross Barclay hooked the ball back into the danger zone, Gunn won a header, and Robinson produced a fine finish on the turn to double the Docker’s advantage.

There was to be no coast to the finish line for Newhaven, though, with the Robins roaring back into the game in the last 20 minutes.

Harvey Blake was inches away from pulling a goal back, with his well-struck effort cannoning off the upright, before Lewis Finney found space in a crowded penalty area to curl the ball beyond the grasp of Rhodes with 13 minutes of normal time left.

Aside from a Robinson effort that was smothered away by the Hassocks custodian, the final stages were largely played out in Newhaven’s defensive half.

With two minutes left of normal time remaining, the visitors seemed almost certain to complete their comeback when a loose ball fell kindly to Finney just inside the six-yard box, only for him to be denied by another superb close-range save by Rhodes.

However, the Dockers managed to cling onto what were a hard-fought but fully-deserved and mightily impressive three-points.

They now look to build on that victory this weekend when Lancing, themselves boosted by a 5-0 win at the weekend, visit Fort Road.

Chelsea have made progress under Xabi Alonso in some areas but in others still look the same chaotic team Enzo Maresca and then Liam Rosenior presided over.

They sit fifth in the table at present and boast one of the Premier League’s most thrilling attacks yet have also dropped points against Hull and lost to both Tottenham and Sunderland, who were bottom of the table at the time.

As the November international break draws to a close, it is time to reassess the progress they have made and the direction of travel under Alonso.

Chelsea’s season began with strong form but in truth has very much been a mixed bag so far.

The victories over Fulham, Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds (in the Carabao Cup) have shown Chelsea at their free-flowing best, but only twice have they kept a Premier League clean sheet so far and there are defensive weaknesses that either need solving or, failing that, disguising by Alonso and his team in the months ahead.

The penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool that saw Chelsea exit the Carabao Cup early was a real disappointment in a season when there is no European football to be had, and it is understandable why plenty of Chelsea fans remain unsure quite what Alonso’s team are and what they want to be, even though they sit fifth in the league.

They have been beaten by Tottenham and Sunderland, neither of which should be games they are losing.

Chelsea made 10 first-team signings in the summer as they totally revamped their squad ready for Alonso’s first season in charge.

By far the best performer among their summer recruits has been Morgan Rogers, who has 11 goal contributions in 13 games for the Blues since his £117million arrival from Aston Villa during the World Cup.

Even though they failed to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day, they did make other recruitments that have looked like proving shrewd signings, including Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix.

It is too early to judge the likes of Danny Welbeck, Emi Martinez and Geovany Quenda. Marco Palestra has been disappointing so far.

It has been a reasonable but not spectacular start to life at Chelsea for Alonso. There have been some decent wins under the Spaniard but also some poor defending and a few performances where it was difficult to detect his tactical influence.

It has been revealed that he has kept his cards close to his chest when speaking to the media but this has felt at times to be a slight obstacle to him developing the strong relationship with Chelsea fans that he and they no doubt want. So has not playing Estevao more.

His team selections were poor against Spurs and Sunderland. It is still early doors for Alonso, who continues to insist Chelsea will look very difficult by the time the season is drawing to a close in May.

At the beginning of the season I predicted that Chelsea would finish fourth, but I have not seen enough from them yet to convince me they will finish quite that high. We’re talking small margins, though, and over the course of 38 league games I do believe they will be good enough to sneak into the Champions League with a fifth-place finish, providing England can claim one of the extra European slots as it always seems to.

Scotland have been branded “boring” under newly introduced head coach Sebastien Pocognoli and urged to rip up their current game plan to get back on track.

Pocognoli, 39, has won just two of his first six games in charge of the national team, and came in for some scathing criticism in the wake of the 4-0 Nations League defeat to Switzerland on Monday night, with many supporters believing the manager is struggling to adapt his tactics to fit the strengths of the squad.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Former Scotland international Don Hutchison believes Pocognoli’s side have looked predictable under their newly introduced manager, and believes the squad must take inspiration from fellow home nation Northern Ireland, who achieved promotion to League A of the Nations League with a battling 1-1 draw away to Hungary on Tuesday night.

“Watching Scotland last night I was bored,” he wrote on his official X account. “Watching the same football I see a hundred times over. Northern Ireland are a good example of not over playing for the sake of it. Why can’t Scotland use a fighting, energy, ratting with “intensity”? Forget this ‘keep ball style’ - it doesn’t suit Scotland.”.

Hutchison, who earned 26 caps for Scotland and is best remembered for scored the winning goal in a 1-0 European Championship playoff second-leg victory over England at Wembley in November 1999, thinks that the current national team are a shining example of what can be achieved when a team plays with more intensity.

Marli Salmon was sent off as England Under-19s fell to a heavy defeat against Austria.

The 17-year-old made his debut for that age group last week in a comfortable win over Slovenia, having been called up as an injury replacement.

However, it was a much more difficult game for Salmon on Tuesday as his afternoon came to a premature end.

The Arsenal defender got the nod against Austria and it was an eventful start to the match, with three goals inside the opening ten minutes.

Austria scored again before half-time to lead 3-1 and that was still the scoreline heading into the final 20 minutes of the match.

Salmon was booked for dissent, having shouted in the referee’s face and waved his arm angrily after conceding a free-kick.

Four minutes later, the teenager was then shown a straight red card to complete a miserable occasion for him.

Reigan Heskey played a loose pass back that left his team-mates scrambling and Salmon could not cut out the danger on the halfway line.

Austria’s Johannes Moser got to the ball first and was running clean through on goal, only for Salmon to slide in and bring him down.

He immediately punched the ground in frustration and did not even look back at the referee, knowing the red card was coming, and he began trudging off the pitch.

Austria went on to score another goal with the man advantage and secure a 4-1 win.

It is the second international break in a row that an Arsenal player has been sent off for the England U19s.

Max Dowman was shown a straight red card last month against the USA for a reckless challenge.

In a recent development, salmon was shown a straight red card for dissent while captaining Arsenal’s Under-21s in a 1-0 defeat by Ipswich Town back in Feburary. He signed his first professional deal with the Gunners in April.

Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm.
  • They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.

According to recent reports, they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining intends and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

It has been revealed that the two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once manufacturer secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

Recent findings suggest that the venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ remarked Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’.

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

In a recent development, ‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he stated: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

Industry observers note that ‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’.

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’.

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

In a recent development, ‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’.

The traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ stated Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’.

Industry observers note that ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ stated Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’.

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a big role in its rise.

Riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’.

Riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’.

His tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ notes Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

The repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

Sources indicate that the benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

In a recent development, ‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he stated.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The challenges you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’.

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ noted Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’.

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

Industry observers note that ‘We need facts or what is called data,’ noted Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country.

‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’.

This is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie said: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’.

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player said to another: “Good game, son”.’.

The football world has thus moved into a newly introduced era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’.

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’.

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for next summer’s Africa Cup of Nations have taken a further hit, after a disappointing goalless draw with Tanzania.

The Super Eagles, who back in the autumn international break were beaten 3-0 by Guinea-Bissau at the Estadio 24 de Setembro, appeared to have got back on track with victory over Tanzania last Friday.

A 3-1 win in Uyo - achieved without Victor Osimhen - coupled with Guinea-Bissau being held to a surprise draw away at Madagascar, was the perfect scenario for Nigeria heading into the reverse fixture at the Amaan Stadium on Tuesday afternoon.

According to recent reports, however, Eric Chelle’s surprising decision to start without Alex Iwobi and Ola Aina in Zanzibar ultimately backfired. Despite dominating possession and creating numerous chances, the Super Eagles simply could not find a breakthrough and will look back at the game as two points dropped.

How costly a 0-0 draw against a side ranked 117th in the world actually is will become clearer after Guinea-Bissau face Madagascar, though it is unlikely that Nigeria will get two favours in the space of four days.

Now, while the result moves Nigeria level on points with Guinea-Bissau in their AFCON 2027 qualification group, they have played a game more and it’s important to remember a runners-up spot may not be enough to advance to next summer’s tournament.

This is because Tanzania have already qualified for AFCON 2027 by virtue of being co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda.

By losing to Guinea-Bissau and drawing with Tanzania in their two away matches so far, Nigeria simply have no margin for error from here on in.

The likely scenario, regardless of the other result on matchday four, is they will have to take six points from their final two matches.

Should Guinea-Bissau beat Madagascar and Tanzania, it will set up a winner-take-all match between the two nations in March 2027 where the Super Eagles will almost certainly find themselves needing to win - and by at least three clear goals.
