📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A five-goal second half blitz underlined the Sports' superior status - but only after the Golds had turned around at half-time at 1-1 and with a glint of an upset in the gleaming, rain-soaked Priory Lane stadium.

Recent findings suggest that george Gaskin and Mitch Hand's squad had made the long trek along the Sussex coast against the background of a frankly awful season so far. They’re a step lower than the Sports, but actually 44 places lower in terms of current league tables.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And if it is ever possible to draw comfort from a 6-1 defeat, they can be satisfied this was a well contested game - which also banished memories of the two clubs' last encounter, an ill-tempered Senior Cup semi-final two seasons ago at Lancing.

Borough had thrown open the gates with free admission at the Connect Management Stadium - and those local football addicts who chose live footy ahead of a warm fireside were actually rather well rewarded.

Steve King's squad is strong on paper but stretched by injuries; but his line-up gave a starting shirt to FA Trophy hero Tyano Wilson as well as young reserve keeper Myles Watkins, and a place on the bench for patient striker Zack Tarrant - who would have the last word of the night.

It has been revealed that wilson created an early chance out of nothing, but his low cross flashed across goal with nobody able to convert. But on just seven minutes, the Sports were ahead: Arthur Grout played a perfectly weighted lofted pass to Liam Nash, who finished in style.

In a recent development, cue a cascade of goals, through the silvery curtain of drizzle under gleaming lights? Nope - or at least not yet. Littlehampton kept their nerve, had a reasonable share of possession and kept their shape.

And, as the minutes drizzled away, half-time was suddenly approaching with the 1-0 scoreline unchanged. And just as suddenly, the Golds grabbed an equaliser through Marcel Powell - smartly taken if only just deserved on the balance of play.

With dressing room doors slammed tightly shut, King and his staff must have passed a few words of wisdom, and the second half saw a more determined and purposeful home performance.

In fact, it took just two minutes from the restart for Max Sheaf to restore the Sports' advantage with a beauty of a strike - and that set the second-half agenda.

Within five minutes, Myles-Watkins produced a strong save at his near post to deny Powell an equaliser. Then Gold Omotayo tucked one under the keeper to extend the home side's lead, or so they thought - but an offside flag chalked it off. No matter: Borough were now controlling most of the play.

Just past the hour, Laleye and Wilson combined beautifully at pace, to set up Gold's tap-in for 3-1. And three minutes later Owen Bellamy - often an unsung hero in the red Borough shirt - curled in the sweetest of strikes from 25 yards, to put the game effectively beyond Littlehampton's reach.

Recent findings suggest that there was still time for Borough's strikers of the future to make their mark. Tarik Kadric and Tarrant enjoyed space against an understandably tiring visiting defence, and after Omotayo had converted a penalty for handball - furiously disputed by the visitors - it was Tarrant who claimed the final goal.

The tall youngster had too much pace for the Golds defence and his strike cannoned in off the underside of the bar.

For Littlehampton, a long and weary drive home, and that ever-ironic agenda to ‘concentrate on the league’. For the Sports, yet another victory - 20 in 22 games - and the ride rolls on.

Gerry Cardinale has clarified his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement from about three years ago, stating that investments and resources are needed to get AC Milan back to the top.

Back in September 2023, a little over a year after he completed the purchase of Milan, Cardinale sat down with Corriere della Sera to explain his project for the club. “In football I want to be a Berlusconi 2.0, to have the same impact as him in a completely changed context,” he remarked, among other things.

Industry observers note that it’s a quote that didn’t land brilliantly with some of the Milan fans, who felt that Cardinale grossly underestimated how much work Berlusconi put in with the throwaway comment. It was more than just a throwaway comment, though.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, following the launch of Milan’s latest holding manufacturer MSE, Cardinale clarified what he meant by the quote. It was not meant as an arrogant comparison, but rather as praise for Berlusconi and what he can learn from the legendary Milan owner.

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected….

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”.

In a recent development, “Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a latest era.

Sources indicate that “We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”.

Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide while playing at Manchester United.

The ex-England striker, who remains United’s record goalscorer, has spoken publicly of his struggles with mental health and alcohol consumption in the past.

But he has now revealed in a candid interview that at his ‘lowest point’ he spent days at home drinking and considered taking his own life.

Speaking on the ‘Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan’ podcast, Rooney explained: “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.”.

“Then I didn’t want (his eldest son) Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

According to recent reports, “I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, (I) really struggled with it.”.

Kai Rooney, the eldest of Wayne’s four children, is now 17 years old and impressing in United’s academy ranks.

Sources indicate that asked to remember the lowest point of his life, Rooney continued: "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink. This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise.".

He added that he “struggled to deal with it all” and acknowledged he “needed help to get through it” after a conversation with his wife Coleen.

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.

Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.

It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.

Back in August 2023, leading official John Beaton addressed calls for greater openness around VAR and gave the impression the refereeing firmament were in favour of a new spirit of glasnost.

‘Anything to explain how we are arriving at decisions and anything we can do to show people what we do on a Saturday and what happens in the VAR centre, we absolutely welcome,’ he said.

It has been revealed that ‘The more transparency, the better. The more questions we get, the more answers we can provide and, we hope, get to a better place,’.

That was followed by new head of refereeing Willie Collum’s VAR show on YouTube the following season. At that point, there seemed a real move to lift the lid and build confidence in our men in black. There was talk of Collum doing his programme more than once a month and suggestions referees might even be open to being interviewed post-match in the right circumstances.

Unfortunately, though, all that has come to nothing and last term — in which controversial decisions had a huge effect on the title race — feels like it could become an obstacle in the way of progress.

Head of Referees Willie Collum should be applauded for speaking up on the SFA VAR show.

It needn’t be, though. There has always been a feeling among referees that being put in front of the cameras carried danger. SFA Ian Maxwell has also spoken about the game being subject to ‘fairly hysterical commentary’ when something bad happens.

In a recent development, the media environment here is nowhere near as febrile as in Spain, though. It has four newspapers dedicated to sport alone. There are countless chat highlights on council telly full of talking heads. Ages ago, news bulletins there had lipreaders telling viewers what coaches and players were saying on the park. Jose Mourinho is also back ruffling officials’ feathers at Real Madrid.

Getting Spanish refs to a place where they feel ready to be interviewed has taken time. It has also taken extra cash for them from TV money and it can still go a lot further.

A selected referee will speak to broadcast rights-holders only. And it’s not after every game. Only selected fixtures.

The SFA made real progress a couple of years back in lifting the curtain and should seek to rediscover that momentum — even though it won’t make the key issue of having to improve overall standards go away.

Sources indicate that since last year, the Spanish FA have been broadcasting their own YouTube show ‘Tiempo de Revision’ to address flashpoints. It should be said that it’s inferior to Collum’s broadcast in terms of content.

It replays incidents against a musical backdrop with captions explaining the decisions. There is no in-game audio, no one like Collum putting himself out there.

Although some of his reasoning for massive calls was a bit suspect last term, that programme remains a platform to build from.

There is no reason why referees shouldn’t explain their decision-making after games here. Criticism they may or may not receive in the aftermath shouldn’t come into it.

If Spanish whistlers can go public, so can they.

Newcastle have made it abundantly clear that they will not allow England international Lewis Hall to leave the club during the January transfer window, according to a report from The Times.

Featuring for England over the past fortnight and appearing to have cemented his spot as Thomas Tuchel’s number one choice at left-back, Hall finds his stock at a red-hot high.

While the Magpies might be searching for some essential Premier League stability on their return from November’s international break this weekend, the 22-year-old has been a standout performer on Tyneside.

Although it might be suggested that Manchester United are keen on reigniting their summer interest when the transfer window reopens, the hierarchy at St. James’ Park have made their stance crystal clear.

The Times reported this week that while Newcastle might be bracing themselves for another pursuit from Man United in January, they will not allow the one-time Chelsea youngster to leave the club under any circumstances.

While Newcastle might have watched the likes of now-former skipper Bruno Guimaraes complete a £75million move to reigning Premier League champions Arsenal over the summer, they have no intention of parting ways with their defensive talisman.

According to recent reports, pledging his future to Newcastle back in September, Hall put pen to paper on a bumper fresh deal at St. James’ Park that is set to run until 2031.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan Women were held to a 3-3 draw in their away game against Napoli on Saturday afternoon, despite having the lead twice.

It has been a rough start to the season for Suzanne Bakker and her side, clinching a mere seven points in the first seven games. Even worse, the form seems to be declining as with today’s game included, they haven’t won in the last three games (1D, 2L).

It has been revealed that in the derby against Inter last week, the Rossonere only had themselves to blame for the 0-3 defeat after missing several good chances, while conceding two penalties and getting a red card. They didn’t exactly make things better today either.

It has been revealed that after just five minutes of play, the former Milan player Chante Dompig opened the scoring for the hosts. In fairness to the Rossonere, it was a cracking finish from outside the box to stun Sally Rainey in goal, so not much could be done.

Sources indicate that milan responded in the best way possible as Sara Kanutte Fornes pounced on a huge mistake by the Napoli defence, tapping in the equaliser after 16 minutes of play. Just ten minutes later, Abi Brighton found the striker on a corner, heading it home nicely for an early brace.

The Rossonere played well after that and headed into the break with a 2-1 lead. It wasn’t a poor start to the second half, but in the 58th minute, a really poor offside trap (of sorts) meant Napoli only had to play one pass to play Kinga Kozak through, and she made no mistakes.

Sloppy defending that Milan thought they had cancelled out in the 78th minute after a lovely move. Thea Kyvåg found Christy Grimshaw in the box with a great cross and the veteran headed it to Emma Koivisto, who in turn headed it into the back of the net.

In a recent development, the lead only lasted about six minutes, though, as Napoli suddenly had loads of space on the right flank and played a smart low cross into the box. Considering the lack of coverage on the flank, the Milan players at least should have kept tabs on things in the box, but they didn’t.

Industry observers note that and so, Michela Giordano made it 3-3 and that was also the final result in the end. Two points dropped for Milan against another struggling side.

Belgium head coach Mark van Bommel shared: “He was ill for a very long time.

It has been revealed that “He has only trained twice since October 17. As a result, he isn’t at 100 per cent, which is why he isn’t part of the squad. He still doesn’t feel quite right, so it was his own choice.”.

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his decision to leave Manchester United in a statement, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to sign the highly-rated young winger.

The 16-year-old has played in United’s academy since 2020 and was expected to start appearing in the first team this season.

Until, that is, he made the shock decision to lodge a transfer request in September, amid reports he and his entourage were frustrated with his lack of first-team opportunities.

Industry observers note that united worked hard to convince him to stay and offered him a new contract, but the player has not trained at the club for some time and is now expected to join Real Madrid. He will leave Old Trafford without having made a senior appearance.

After months of speculation as to where he might end up, Gabriel has now issued the clearest upgrade yet on his situation, confirming his decision to leave United in a post to his Instagram page.

Speaking over clips of himself playing for the club, he said: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with massive dreams.

“Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

“To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”.

Gabriel has reportedly been training alone in Madrid while waiting for his move away from United to be ratified.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

Tributes are pouring in for Arsenal legend Peter Storey, who has passed away at the age of 81.

The Surrey-born midfielder, who retired with 19 England caps, first joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and went on to play a vital role in the side which won a league and FA Cup double in 1971.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy. He also lifted the Fairs Cup with the club.

Initially a full-back, he was later moved into midfield, where he spent the remainder of his career and gained a reputation as a crunching tackler.

It has been revealed that storey made 501 appearances in total for Arsenal and is their eighth all-time highest appearance maker. He left north London in 1977 to sign with Fulham before retiring in 1978.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund, which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double Winner, Peter Storey.

“All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.”.

Storey’s family added in a statement: "We are deeply saddened by the loss of Peter, a much-loved father and grandfather. He is survived by his three sons and grandchildren, who will miss him dearly. We are deeply grateful for the many kind messages, tributes and good wishes we have received.

“It has been a great comfort to see the affection and respect in which he was held by so many, both within the football community and beyond.".

England also paid tribute on their official X account, adding: “We are saddened to learn that Peter Storey – who won 19 caps for the Three Lions in the 1970s – has passed away at the age of 81.

“Our condolences are with Peter’s family and friends at this time.”.

Storey hung up his boots when his Fulham contract was cancelled, just eight months after he had signed. He went on to own a north London pub.

He was convicted of a number of criminal offences after retiring from football, including smuggling pornography, keeping a brothel, and financing the production of counterfeit coins, as detailed in his 2010 autobiography ‘True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man’.

Additional reporting: Press Association.

Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026.

Boston was the loveliest little holiday romance. An unforgettable moment in time. But let’s just leave it at that, shall we?

Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?

Or does everything have to be milked to the max these days? Flogged like a dead horse to benefit someone or other. Ruined, really. Played out until every scintilla of fun has been drained out of it.

A bit like Yes, Sir, I Can Boogie. That started out as a bona-fide hoot. A half-cut Andy Considine dressing up in drag with his friends and family during his stag do in London in 2015 and making a music video around Baccara’s 1977 hit. It went viral. Obviously. It was – and is – hilarious.

When Scotland’s players resurrected it in the dressing room in Serbia five years later – with Considine as part of the squad – after the national team had ended a 23-year wait to make it to a major competition, it was simply inspired.

Every second of those infectious scenes exuded elation, joy, togetherness and pin-sharp humour, a killer recipe for the interludes that make life and living so great.

Recent findings suggest that now? Even the opening bars of the song bring on a sense of dread. It was splattered over T-shirts, played everywhere on repeat and still gets aired at every Scotland home game.

The Tartan Army march to Boston's Fenway Park baseball stadium.

In a recent development, it’s boring. It’s been done to death and now lives firmly in that grim, stagnant swamp known as Scottish mainstream culture along with munchy boxes, Bitz N Pieces, theatre reveals about the Old Firm and ex-footballers suddenly developing a personality and getting involved in stage shows to tell the world how Wee Dazza once did Big Jazza a beauty in the dressing-room by leaving a squelchy banana in his shoe. The banter anawrat.

Everything ends up spoiled here and it looks like we’re already well down that road with the Tartan Army thanks to the news breaking that the Scottish FA are in talks with the State of Massachusetts over a biennial friendly match at the Gillette Stadium, the black hole amid the festivity at the finals thanks to struggling past Haiti and embarrassing ourselves against Morocco.

It has been revealed that state senator Paul Feeney has been across the pond to press the flesh. Massachusetts senate president Karen Spilka is already talking about staging Tartan Day – presumably some rip-off of that twee, shortbread-tin abomination in Newly introduced York – and ‘other events’.

Recent findings suggest that the heart sinks. Listen, the minute politicians get involved in any kind of ‘happening’, the best thing to do is give it a wide berth.

Mind you, before the Significant Swerve, it might be worthwhile having someone remind these characters from The Bay State that Massachusetts’ first contribution to Scotland supporters hitting town in summer involved hiking the cost of the 25-mile train ride from Boston to the ground from $20 to a ludicrous $80.

What unfolded there in mid-June was nothing to do with them. It was everything to do with spontaneity. As it ought to be. A glorious coming-together of all sorts of folk up for a right, royal carry-on.

There were so many glorious vignettes. Scotland punters taking over Red Sox games. Bars running out of beer. Mass marches. Local women, doped-up on Outlander, telling TikTok how a bunch of jakeys intent on drinking anything within arm’s reach – except Bud Light, of course – were making them feel ‘seen’.

The Tartan Army make their presence known in Boston during the summer's World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that it was brilliant. A short spell in which stars aligned and magic happened. Boston had everything the Tartan Army required. And going by the testimony of Bostonians, the Tartan Army brought badly needed vitality back to the streets of a city quietened by Covid and other factors.

In a recent development, everybody won. Everyone there still dines out on the memory. But that’s where it should stay. In the memory. These conversations about trying to recapture that spirit, recreate it every two years around some meaningless friendly against opposition unconfirmed and possible business meetings on the periphery, feel quite sad. How can it have any legs long-term?

Joe and Josephine Punter have moved on. They’re on the batter in other places now. Next week, it’s Switzerland for a Nations League game. After that, it’s wherever the draw for the Euro qualifiers throws them. Fresh cities. New adventures. As football away days ought to be. In, out, shake it all about.

Away days are not about teaming up with suit-wearing dignitaries to be paraded at the town hall, like performing seals in plaid – even though there does appear to be an element of the Scotland support that enjoys that kind of thing.

Away days are not about being used as political capital or forming part of some constructed ‘festival’.

Look, in most aspects of life, it’s generally best not to go back. Sticking traffic cones on top of statues all over town won’t be as funny next time. There won’t be a 20,000-strong travelling support spending their life savings on games an entire generation had been waiting for. There won’t be anything like the same buzz, if any.

Some folk might fancy returning once, just to see if it feels the same. The idea that this is going to be a big deal every two years, though, feels deeply misguided.

Boston’s Irish. Not Scottish. That Tartan Week nonsense in Latest York is a toe-curlingly awful melange of kilts, Scottie dogs and actors living in America telling everyone back home how to vote.

According to recent reports, no self-respecting Scot should give it house room. If there is a strategy for the same thing in Boston, the same rules apply.

Like NYC, it’ll suit those from the political class in the mood for a junket, of course. John Swinney will already be counting the air miles if there’s another game in Massachusetts to go to.

The public, of course, is still counting the cost of the First Minister’s last trip there for the World Cup. The bill came in at £45,000 for him and two senior aides to fly business class. The entire trip for government staff came to more than £98,000.

Swinney plays the role with aplomb at these affairs, supping a pint in his Scotland top. The Scottish Football Association need to ask themselves this, though: why should they put themselves at the heart of some kind of cock-eyed project to build bridges politically?

The Tartan Army leave their signature traffic cone in a park in Boston.

Recent findings suggest that first up, the players are hardly likely to welcome a pointless week in America being added to a jam-packed schedule. More importantly, though, what exactly has this SNP-led administration, outwith giving a few bob to grassroots, done for Scottish football down the years?

According to recent reports, from this vantage point, they’ve been no friend to the national game or its followers. The Offensive Behaviour at Football Act, repealed in 2018, was a scandalous piece of legislation that criminalised fans and made going to football unpleasant.

Clubs have had to fight tooth and nail to secure trials to sell pints inside stadiums when other sports are allowed to do what they like. After trouble in Glasgow city centre ahead of the Old Firm League Cup final two years ago, Swinney stated that ‘the clubs have got a responsibility to make sure their fans behave properly’.

Inside their grounds, yes. What are they meant to do, though, about teenagers running amok on Argyle Street?

Looking after that is the job of the police. Of course, anyone reading 1919 magazine, funded by the Scottish Police Federation, earlier this year will have noted an article about policing around football being ‘chaotic’ and understaffed because of SNP Government budget cuts.

Just like everything else in this sorry little nation built on buying votes for ‘free stuff’, Police Scotland is creaking at the seams. Why would anyone want to get involved in another transatlantic piece of theatre selling some false, outdated, vaguely comical vision of it to foreigners?

A pointless Scotland friendly – served up as part of some forced, hackneyed ‘cultural exchange’ or not – is hardly an idea to be getting on board with.

Sources indicate that pure dead brilliant, it won’t be. More like pure cringe.

The beleaguered Oakwell outfit find themselves second from bottom in League One ahead of Friday night's televised home derby with Sheffield Wednesday.

Winless in nine league matches since September 2, the Reds are only kept off the foot of the table by goal difference. They have taken just two points from the last available 27.

Barnsley must make do without McGeehan on Friday after he picked up his fifth league booking of the season.

The return from international duty of Northern Ireland's Patrick Kelly will at least soften the blow.

But the goalscoring nous of McGeehan (pictured), who netted his ninth goal of the season in Saturday's reverse at fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic in a crunch Roses fixture, will be an undoubted miss.

McGeehan's derby role will revolve around rallying a young group of players and he has stressed that the Reds squad must start showing more appetite for the survival fight.

On the task ahead for Barnsley, who last played in the old fourth division in 1978-79, said: "We've got to fight.

"We're in a dogfight. We've got to be prepared every time we go out now to fight more than we have been because we're letting ourselves down at the minute.

"We've got to fight more and more. That's all we can do.

"Fight for the shirt and we'll turn it around.".

Part of a Northampton Town side who were relegated last term, McGeehan, 31, is personally motivated to avoid that fate for a second successive year.

"It hurts us all," he continued.

Recent findings suggest that "It's our jobs. It's our life. We live for it.

It has been revealed that "We come in every day. We're always thinking about it. We take it home with us every night.

"We understand the fans have every right to be frustrated.

"We've got a huge game at home against our local rivals.

"If there's ever a game to turn it around, it's that game.".

Wednesday are set to be backed by a travelling contingent of 5,310 supporters at Oakwell.

The Owls quickly sold out their initial allocation and a further 500 tickets were made available from 2pm on Tuesday.

Sweden boss Graham Potter was quick to defend Dejan Kulusevski after the forward’s form in this international break was criticised.

It has been revealed that tottenham forward Kulusevski only recently returned from an extended injury layoff. In May 2025, he suffered a complex patella injury and endured a lengthy recovery pockmarked with various setbacks and multiple surgical procedures.

The 26-year-old made a long-awaited comeback earlier this autumn, though, and has now made four cameo appearances for Tottenham.

Those showings were enough to earn him a recall to Potter’s Sweden squad for the November international break, where he has enjoyed substitute appearances totalling 56 minutes in a victory over Bosnia & Herzegovina and a draw with Poland, his first appearances for his nation since November 2024.

Recent findings suggest that his performances this month, though, have been criticised by some in the Swedish press. The outlet TVmatchen dubbed his performance against Bosnia “miserable”, adding: “For obvious reasons not in absolute match form, but looked slow and was never in the game. Was he really ready for this already?”.

The news site Svenskafans then described him as “eager” but “rusty”.

Potter, though, has leapt to Kulusevski’s defence, slamming what he considers unwarranted criticism.

“I think the criticism is completely unfair, to be honest,” he told Viaplay following Tuesday’s draw with Poland.

He continued, explaining why he felt Kulusevski was ready to return to the Blagult fold: “He has trained very, very well. You have to judge someone based on a match like that, like it was against Bosnia. It wasn't easy for the substitutes to come into that match.

According to recent reports, “Now he just needs to get playing time, and that's completely normal. It's completely normal for anyone who's been out with an injury and is now getting back into match form.”.

Kulusevski has yet to score or assist since returning to first-team action, but is only expected to increase his involvement for club and country as he builds back his fitness in the coming weeks.

Speaking last week, Potter acknowledged the need to be gentle with Kulusevski, and he worked with Tottenham to ensure he was not overexerted during the November break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino could be boosted by some returnees as he faces the first match of his Manchester United tenure on Sunday.

Today, Wednesday, November 18, is officially the first day of the Argentine’s tenure with United, and once he arrives at Carrington he will throw himself headlong into preparing for his first match.

That will come just five days after his arrival in the form of a trip to Anfield, to face Liverpool.

High on his to-do list will be figuring out who is or is not fit to make that journey across the north-west, and there is no shortage of patients in the physio’s room.

Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba are the most notable absentees, but Pochettino stands to welcome a number of fit-again stars back into the squad this week.

With that in mind, here is all the latest Manchester United injury news and potential return dates...

Marcus Rashford has not featured for United since the defeat by Atletico Madrid in October, when he picked up a persistent hip matter.

He had been pushing to return against Aston Villa but did not feature in the matchday squad, and has spent the international break building up his fitness at Carrington.

Michael Carrick had described Rashford’s injury as “day-by-day” before he left the United job, and it is hoped he will be able to return at Anfield.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A).

Luke Shaw has been sidelined with a muscle injury since early October, but is thought to be pushing for a return to fitness.

As of the Aston Villa draw, Shaw had yet to return to training, but reports during the international break suggest he is pushing for a comeback at Anfield.

His return would be a huge boost for Pochettino and United, given the squad lacks a clear backup for Shaw at left-back.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A).

The summer signing Carlos Baleba has made a stuttering start to this campaign as he struggles for fitness.

He arrived from Brighton with an ankle injury, which he shook off to make a run of appearances, before tweaking his hamstring against Roma earlier this month.

Speaking at the time, Carrick explained Baleba is facing weeks out and would not return during the international break.

Potential return date: December 2026.

Patrick Dorgu missed a stretch of this campaign after suffering a hamstring injury in the September international break, but returned to put in an impressive cameo against Aston Villa last time out.

According to recent reports, it seems, though, that he is not yet fully fit. He joined up with the Danish national team for the November international break and traied with his team-mates, but was promptly sent home due to fitness concerns.

“He's still on his way back. The fact that he got those minutes against Aston Villa and did a fantastic job should be taken with a grain of salt,” said head coach Brian Riemer. “There are still some lingering issues with the major muscle injury he suffered. We need to make sure it doesn't flare up again. We're optimistic, and we also believe things will go well.”.

A statement issued by the Danish FA when he left camp said he was not match fit, but it is hoped he will be able to feature in the Anfield match.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A).

Harry Maguire was forced off at half-time of the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa with a back injury.

He had come into the match with a knock but pushed through it to start, but did not last long thereafter.

Carrick explained it was a back spasm which forced hi off, adding: "I don't know how bad it is but, going into the internationals, there should be plenty of time for him to recover.".

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A).

Benjamin Sesko has been ruled out until the new year with a niggling shin injury.

The major Slovenian missed the latter stages of last season and the early days of the current campaign after suffering an injury at Old Trafford in May.

He enjoyed a run in the side and appeared to be back at full fitness, but has since been sidelined again having reaggravated the initial problem.

It is hoped a lengthy rest will allow him to fully recover without undergoing surgery.

Speaking before being sacked, Carrick said: “We're not exactly sure yet how long [he will be out for], but it's going to be a significant amount of time, unfortunately.

“So I feel for Ben, he had the issue at the end of last season that we looked after and tried to give him as much time to recover and then unfortunately he's had the issue coming into this season.

“So, we've got to do what's best for Ben and he's going to have to have some time on the sidelines, unfortunately.

Potential return date: January 2027.

Manuel Ugarte is right now recovering after undergoing surgery on a ruptured ACL suffered at the World Cup. He is expected to miss most, if not all, of the 2026/27 season.

Potential return date: Summer 2027.
